required_outcomes: Replies to the tenant in writing on the garden with an honest status (landlord approval still outstanding, a contractor arranged through Oakley has looked at the garden, no works date) and a date for the next update.
Chases the landlord (Jenkins) in writing for his decision on the garden, since phone calls have gone unanswered, saying what is needed and by when.
Treats the dripping kitchen mixer tap as a new routine repair separate from the garden request: logs it as its own job, or asks the one fact needed to log it, and tells the tenant.
Also answers the other points briefly (parking permit, rent receipt, bins) without inventing facts the record does not hold.
acceptable_alternatives: Pointing the tenant to the council for the parking permit, or saying the agency will check and come back.
Saying the rent receipt will be confirmed by the accounts team, rather than confirming payment without a record of it.
Chasing Oakley for her contractor quote as well as the landlord.
positive_behaviours: Structures the reply so each of the five points gets an answer.
Acknowledges that the bins report needs no action from the agency.
Records that calls to the landlord have gone unanswered since 8 February and sets a follow-up date.
red_flags: Answering only the garden question and ignoring the tap.
Confirming the March rent was received when nothing in the record shows it.
prohibited_actions: Telling the tenant the landlord has approved the garden work.
Assigning a contractor or instructing works on the garden.
critical_failures: Giving the tenant a garden works date or a tap visit date that nothing in the record supports.
